statement: A 2026 study reports that late Neanderthals in northwestern Europe were not inbred and had greater genetic diversity than earlier low-diversity population estimates suggested, complicating the "genetically doomed by inbreeding/low diversity" strand of the extinction narrative for at least this regional population.

sources.citation: "Genetic diversity of late Neanderthals in northwestern Europe." Nature (2026) — author list not independently confirmed in this research pass.
sources.access_note: Single recent paper; full author list and independent replication not yet confirmed.

does_not_demonstrate: that the broader small-population/low-diversity picture is wrong for Neanderthals generally — this finding is regionally and temporally specific to late northwestern European Neanderthals
notes: Confidence set LOW: single very recent (2026) finding, not yet cross-checked against independent replication or full field response in this research pass.
